_meta.description: Every setting the server owns: server-wide, per-workspace, and per-device rows the server stores. Hand-maintained copy of the registry in server/src/settings/registry.ts; server/tests/settings-registry.test.ts requires both to list the same keys with the same scope, storage, default and revisioned. Change a row together with its registry entry. The Apple client declares its settings in OppiCore/Settings/SettingsCatalog.swift, and SettingsCatalogContractTests requires every server-backed declaration to match a row here: its scope, its field, and its revisioned flag.
_meta.scope: server = one value for the whole server; workspace = one value per workspace; device = one value per paired device, stored on the server.
_meta.storage: config = config.json; settings-file = <dataDir>/settings/*.json; workspace = the workspace record; pi = Pi's settings.json (the terminal sees it too); push-registration = the device's stored push registration.
_meta.default: null means no value to default to: derived when the workspace is created, owned by Pi, or required on write.
_meta.revisioned: true means the stored value carries a revision the API returns. autoTitle, serverMetrics and mobileOutputGuide save with an optional baseRevision (mobileOutputGuide requires it); a stale one answers 409 { error, code: "revision_conflict", current } and leaves the setting unchanged. The dictionaries keep their own contract: PUT carries `revision`, a stale one answers 409 { error }.

settings.validation: PUT /server/auto-title takes a partial object; enabled must be a boolean; model must be provider/id and resolve in the server's model runtime, or null to clear it.
PUT /server/metrics/settings takes enabled as a boolean.
PUT /server/mobile-output-guide takes exactly enabled (boolean) and baseRevision.
At most 100 phrases; each trimmed, non-empty, without control characters, at most 256 UTF-8 bytes; no repeats.
The same phrase rules as dictionaryGlobal, kept per workspace.

settings.type: { allowedHosts?: string[], env?: Record<string, string>, mcpServers?: string[] } | null
settings.validation: An object with only allowedHosts (strings), env (string values) and mcpServers (names of letters, digits, _ and -); null clears it on update.
